profile.campus: Lewisville, Denton County, Texas (CyrusOne DFW2 campus)
profile.address: 2501 South State Highway 121, Suite 500, Lewisville, TX 75067
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, DFW2 sits at 2501 South State Highway 121, Suite 500, Lewisville, TX 75067, publishing 200,000 sq ft and 12 MW of total IT capacity.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten; the company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro is anchored by CyrusOne's Carrollton (DFW1) facility, which Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry describes the company itself calling the largest data center in Texas when it opened in 2012, and today spans additional DFW-numbered buildings in Allen and Lewisville; Texas's absence of a state corporate income tax and its position as a major interstate fiber crossroads have helped make the state, alongside Northern Virginia, one of CyrusOne's largest concentrations of US facilities.

In 2016, CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, a transaction illustrating the sale-leaseback and anchor-tenant financing structures common among large colocation operators. Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued to expand its US footprint, including the January 2025 groundbreaking of a new fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6) representing roughly $1 billion in cumulative San Antonio capital investment per the company's own materials, indicating continued growth investment in Texas markets under private ownership rather than a slowdown following the take-private transaction.

reading.body:
CyrusOne DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet in Lewisville, a suburb on the northern edge of the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 12 MW of IT load is roughly 300 racks, enough to run a modest GPU cluster but not a hyperscale training environment. At 10 kW per rack, a more typical mixed-enterprise density, the same power supports around 1,200 racks. The operator does not publish power density targets, so neither figure is their claim.

The certifications qualify this campus to host regulated workloads. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies the information security management system against an international standard. FISMA qualifies it to support U.S. federal agency workloads. SSAE 16 Type II is an audited controls report that satisfies many enterprise procurement requirements. TIA-942 is a data center infrastructure design standard, with tier level not published here.

Within Texas, this site ranks seventh among the eight facilities on this site for which a megawatt figure is published, out of 133 mapped facilities in the state total. Those eight published facilities sum to 315 MW, and DFW2's 12 MW represents roughly 3.8 percent of that disclosed total. Texas is a significant data center state by count, but most operators there publish no capacity figure, so the 315 MW baseline almost certainly understates the real installed base. DFW2 is a mid-sized, compliance-oriented facility, not a leading indicator of AI scaling capacity in the region.
